title: Reconcile RigLock's scope: switch `Local\` to `Global\` with a cross-session test, or correct the 'machine-wide' claims
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: RigLock's mutex is switched from `Local\` to `Global\` (machine-wide scope): missing
A cross-session test exists proving RigLock serialises (or fails loudly for) two runs from different sign-in sessions: missing
The builder's account / SmbRig.cs comments claiming 'machine-wide' are corrected to state the true per-sign-in-session scope: partial

The design deliberately left out the Global\ switch and the cross-session test. The build-check's two 'missing' items are the rejected branch of an either/or slice, not unfinished work. A cross-session test cannot run unattended here (spike 1: the sandbox refuses the S4U scheduled task).

Engine: a design's architecture_rules append writes neither `including_comments` nor `(?m)`. So any declared rule about comment or prose text is dead on arrival, and SL-059's design fell into exactly this. Either the design schema carries including_comments, or design-slice is told that comment-only patterns never fire by default.

O-006 needs a person. With a second sign-in session (Fast User Switching or an S4U task started by hand), check whether an SMB mapping made in one session appears in Get-SmbMapping in the other. Only then is 'a per-session lock covers everything the sweep can touch' measured rather than recalled.

The person-run network pass (WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork, then Core.Tests filtered to Network=SMB-LOOPBACK) is stale. It already was since eafb1c3, and SL-059 touches SmbRig.cs, StallRig, StalledShareTests and WindowCases.ps1 again. A person should re-run it and record the HEAD.

Several comments call the SMB mappings 'the machine's' or 'this machine's': SmbRig.cs:16, WindowCases.ps1:22/627/3331, SL-020-scanner.md:216. If O-006's recalled premise holds (mappings belong to a logon session), these overstate scope in the same way the RigLock comments did. They are not about RigLock and were left alone per C-003. They are a candidate for a small wording slice once O-006 is measured.

not reached: Cross-session behaviour of the lock itself. The doc now states that Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig is not seen from another session, and that Global\ would be. Both come from recalled Microsoft semantics; spike 2 cases (a), (b) and (c) never ran.

not reached: Whether the SMB client's 'one port per server name' limit for 127.0.0.1 applies per logon session or across the whole machine. If it is machine-wide, two rig runs in different sessions could still clash at the redirector even though the lock does not serialise them. The doc names the lock's scope but not this.
